text: When you rest, God works. When you work, God rests.
explanation:
Moses stood with the Red Sea in front and Pharaoh's chariots closing in behind. Every instinct said do something. God said, "Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord… The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace." Literally: see the Yeshua of the Lord. Centuries later, Jehoshaphat heard the same words: "You will not need to fight in this battle. Position yourselves, stand still and see."

Standing still isn't natural, but it's how grace works. Law is man working; grace is God working. The moment you stop striving and rest in Him, He steps in, and seas part.

text: Jehoshaphat's battlefield was renamed the Valley of Berachah, "blessing." It took three days to carry away the spoil.
explanation:
Judah faced a vast invading army. Jehoshaphat sent singers ahead praising, "Praise the Lord, for His mercy endures forever," and the Lord set ambushes so the enemy armies destroyed one another. When Judah arrived, there was so much plunder that "they were three days gathering the spoil." On the fourth day they assembled in that valley and blessed the Lord, and it's still called the Valley of Berachah, blessing.

The valley where the battle was supposed to happen became the valley of blessing. Whatever valley you're facing (sickness, job loss, fear), God can rename it. Keep praising His enduring mercy, and expect to come out carrying spoil.

text: Jesus died to sin once for all. Not its power, which never held Him, but its guilt and condemnation. So did you.
explanation:
"For the death that He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life that He lives, He lives to God. Likewise you also, reckon yourselves to be dead indeed to sin." Dying to sin isn't a daily struggle; it happened once, in Him. But in what sense did Jesus die to sin? Sin never had power over Him, so He didn't die to its power. He died to its guilt, its judgment and its condemnation, because He bore yours.

That's how you're dead to sin: sin can never again bring condemnation or punishment on you. As one theologian put it, if sin isn't crucified in your conscience, it won't be crucified in your heart. Settle it in your conscience, and you'll find its pull weakening.

text: "Those who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life." Receive is continuous: keep receiving.
explanation:
"If by the one man's offence death reigned through the one, much more those who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ." Death's reign is total; no one escapes it. But much more, grace reigns. And "receive" is in the continuous present: those who keep on receiving.

It's a gift, so you can't earn it. Try hard to be extra patient today, and see how badly it goes. Many people trapped in addictions have found freedom by declaring, even in the middle of their struggle, "I am the righteousness of God in Christ." Over time, the desire just fell away. You can't receive abundance of grace if you only hear a trickle of it. Keep hearing; keep receiving; reign.

text: Adoni-Bezek kept seventy kings under his table, thumbs and big toes cut off. Kings who couldn't grip or stand.
explanation:
Before he was defeated by Judah, the Canaanite king Adoni-Bezek had seventy captured kings gathering scraps under his table. With their thumbs cut off, they couldn't hold a sword; with their big toes gone, they couldn't stand firm or run. They were still kings, but they couldn't reign.

That's a picture of believers who are royalty in Christ but live defeated, picking up crumbs. Interestingly, when priests were consecrated, the blood and then the oil were applied to the right ear, right thumb and right big toe. Your hearing, your handling and your walk are anointed. Receive grace and righteousness, and rise from under the table to reign in life.

text: Jesus crossed a stormy lake for one tormented man, and with one word, a legion of demons left.
explanation:
The man of the Gadarenes lived among the tombs, crying out night and day and cutting himself with stones. On a still day, sound carries across the Sea of Galilee; perhaps Jesus heard those cries from Capernaum. He crossed the lake through a storm the enemy stirred up, just to reach that one man, and with a single command the whole legion fled.

Afterwards, the man begged to go with Jesus. Jesus sent him home instead: "Tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how He has had compassion on you." He became an evangelist across ten cities. No one is too far gone for Jesus to cross a sea for.

text: Every morning, say: "Something good is going to happen to me today."
explanation:
After offering one sacrifice for sins forever, Jesus sat down at God's right hand, "from that time waiting till His enemies are made His footstool." Seated and expecting: that's the throne attitude. Those who reject Him live with "a certain fearful expectation of judgment." But Bible hope (elpis) is a confident expectation of good.

So rest, and switch on your expectancy. "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life" — all of them, not just the good ones. When you wake up, say, "This is the day the Lord has made," and expect His goodness. You'll recognise it when it comes.
